content.learning_goal: Teach learners to understand and apply the main ideas of 'Earth — Our Shared Home'.

explanation_sections.title: Connect
explanation_sections.explanation: Begin with learners' prior experience related to Earth — Our Shared Home and invite predictions.

explanation_sections.title: Explore
explanation_sections.explanation: Use the chapter evidence below to build the explanation rather than introducing unsupported facts.
source_evidence: The Blue Planet “After seeing the Earth from outside the first thought that came to mind was that, the Earth looks completely one, no border is visible from outside.
It seems that no border exists, no state exists, no countries exist.

We all are part of humanity and the Earth is our one home, and all of us are in it.” These were the inspiring words shared by Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, the first Indian to reach the International Space Station, during his conversation with the then Prime Minister of India.
Earth — Our Shared Home10 Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma, the Indian astronaut, was the first Indian to see the Earth from space.

explanation_sections.title: Make meaning
explanation_sections.explanation: Ask learners to explain what the evidence shows, compare ideas, and justify answers.

explanation_sections.title: Apply
explanation_sections.explanation: Move from a chapter example to a new, closely related example.

teaching_sequence.teacher_action: Model close reading/working with the chapter.

teaching_sequence.student_action: Explain why an answer is supported.

misconceptions: Giving an answer without explaining the reasoning.
checks_for_understanding: What evidence in 'Earth — Our Shared Home' supports your answer?
Can you explain the idea in your own words?
content.closure: Ask the learner to state the most important idea and one way it can be used.
